“Sakura.”

I call through the door.

No answer comes from the changing room.

More than that—I cannot sense anyone inside at all.

…The sound grows steadily heavier, my gentle tapping becoming a violent pounding.

…Perhaps it was foolish to worry, but I am simply glad nothing happened.

A bath and a full night’s sleep should restore Sakura’s health.

振り向かず、片手をヒラヒラとあげて話しかける。
pages.en:
“Um, Shirou…?”

“I’ll stay a little longer. You’ll become used to the room soon enough, and I’ll leave once you fall asleep.

“Honestly, I’m worried you’ll push yourself again. I’ll be watching you for another thirty minutes, so lie down and behave.”

Without turning, I raise one hand in a careless wave.

A soft breeze brushes my cheek.

It must be the air stirred by Sakura pulling the covers around herself.

…Well, if this is enough to calm her, it costs me nothing.

Compared with everything Sakura has done for me, it does not amount even to interest.

pages.en:
“————”

“————”

Only the second hand of the clock sounds in the darkness.

Perhaps because my back is turned, or perhaps because of the timid profile Sakura showed me moments ago, the feelings that surged through me when I lifted her have fallen silent.

Now I simply watch the clock in peace.

…Silence endures until it seems we must both have fallen asleep.

I answer with nothing more than a nod.

Apparently satisfied, Sakura releases a quiet breath.

“…Good. Thank you for today.”

And slowly, gently, she descends into sleep.
